jurisdiction: West Contra Costa Unified School District
title: Parcel tax
question: Shall the measure supporting local quality education in West Contra Costa Unified School District, protecting core academics, science, music, arts, and career technical programs that prepare students for the changing economy; attracting and retaining qualified teachers; and maintaining mental health services and counselors to support student success; by renewing the parcel tax at the existing rate of 7.2¢/building square foot, raising approximately $10,238,737 annually for nine years, with senior exemptions, independent citizen oversight, audits, and local control, be adopted?
analysis: The governing board of the West Contra Costa Unified School District has adopted a resolution proposing to extend its current parcel tax (a qualified special tax). This ballot measure asks voters to decide whether an existing parcel tax should continue to be imposed on parcels of taxable real property within the District for nine years, beginning July 1, 2027 and expiring on June 30, 2036.

If the measure passes, the tax would apply to each “improved parcel” of taxable real property in the District. An improved parcel, property with a building on it, would be taxed at a rate of 7.2 cents per square foot of total building area on the parcel. For example, the annual tax on a parcel with a 2,000 square-foot building would be $144.

Based on information from the County Auditor-Controller’s Office, the current parcel tax applying the same rate of 7.2 cents per square foot of total building area per parcel is set to expire on June 30, 2027.

The ballot measure includes certain exemptions. Upon proper application to the District, the District may exempt any parcel from the parcel tax that is owned and occupied as a principal residence by (1) a person 65 years of age or older; (2) a person receiving Supplemental Security Income for a disability; or (3) a person receiving Social Security Disability Insurance benefits, whose yearly income does not exceed 250 percent of the 2012 federal poverty guidelines issued by the United States Department of Health and Human Services.

The ballot measure states that the proceeds of the parcel tax will be used for “protecting core academics, science, music, arts and career technical programs that prepare students for the changing economy; attracting and retaining qualified teachers; and maintaining mental health services and counselors to support student success.” Proceeds from the parcel tax may be used only for the specific purposes set forth in the ballot measure and according to constitutional and statutory provisions.

State law requires the District’s chief fiscal officer to file an annual report with the District’s Board of Education that states the amounts of funds collected and expended in each year and the status of any projects required or authorized to be funded from the parcel tax proceeds. The proceeds from the parcel tax will be deposited into a District account that will be kept separate from other District accounts. Parcel tax funds will be subject to an annual financial audit. The measure also requires the District to have an independent oversight committee to oversee the use of parcel tax proceeds.
Of those voting on the measure, two-thirds must approve the measure for it to pass.
A “yes” vote is in favor of authorizing the parcel tax for a nine-year period.
A “no” vote is against authorizing the parcel tax for a nine-year period.
arg_for: A Yes vote on Measure V will preserve vital funds for local schools. It is not a new tax; it will renew local education funding and continue our investment in West Contra Costa students.

Measure V will continue local funding that has supported our students and our schools since 2004 with no rate increase. Measure V will raise $10.2 million annually. Every dollar remains in our community and cannot be taken by the state or federal government.

California funding has not kept pace with rising costs for special education, employee salaries, utilities, insurance, and essential school operations. Without renewal, our schools face cuts to programs students rely on every day.
A Yes vote helps by:
• Protecting core academics in reading, writing, math, and science
• Maintaining science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) instruction
• Attracting and retaining qualified teachers
• Providing career and technical training to prepare students for careers in a changing economy
• Maintaining mental health and counseling services
• Supporting visual and performing arts
• Improving campus safety
• Supporting athletic and sports programs
• Supporting after school programs

Measure V includes strong taxpayer protections. Independent citizen oversight ensures funds are spent as promised, with annual audits by a state-approved certified public accountant. Revenue stays local and cannot be used for administrator salaries. Seniors and qualified individuals with disabilities remain eligible for an exemption.

Strong schools build strong communities. They strengthen our neighborhoods, prepare our future workforce, and help make West Contra Costa a community where families and businesses want to invest. We all benefit from strong schools.
Protect what we have built and invest in our future.
Vote Yes on Measure V – vital funds for local schools.
Visit www.VoteYesOnV.com

arg_against: Vote No on Measure V.
The West Contra Costa Unified School District (WCCUSD) does not have a revenue problem.
● The 2026-27 budget shows anticipated revenue of $532 Million, with expected spending of $520 Million — an operating surplus of $12 million.
● Since 2016-17, enrollment has declined from 28,518 to 24,423 — more than 4,000 students!

● So WCCUSD will spend $21,304 for each of its 2026-27 estimated 24,423 enrolled students, on record state funding levels. Per-student funding based on projected “Average Daily Attendance” (ADA) of 22,677 students is even higher.

● Measure V would now extend a parcel tax first imposed in 2004 to 2036, having annually taken $10 Million extra for 32 years by then, and guaranteeing the district an extra $10 million every year, no matter how much lower WCCUSD enrollments drop.
Consider what WCCUSD residents already pay:

● The highest school-bond tax in Contra Costa County, about $254 per $100,000 of assessed value (stacked from bonds passed in 2000, 2002, 2005, 2010, 2012, and 2020), and 3½ times Mt. Diablo Unified’s $72.
● Some of the highest sales taxes in the Bay Area, 10.75% percent in El Cerrito and 9.75% percent in Richmond, against California’s 7.25% statewide base.
● A West Contra Costa Healthcare District parcel tax of $52 per home (higher for other properties), still collected years after Doctors Medical Center closed in 2015.
Now consider the district’s direction:

● Spending has climbed to $520 million in 2026-27 from $377 million in COVID Year 2019-20 (a 38% increase), even as enrollment has fallen 13.5 percent over those years, from 28,247 students then to 24,423 now.
A “No” vote on Measure V takes not a dollar from other record funding the schools already receive. Voting “No” requires a district already running a surplus to live within its means.
Enough is enough. Vote No on V.
Contra Costa Tax Payers Association, Denise Gianni, Member of Executive Committee
Lyle Miller, Retired Business Owner, San Pablo
Robin MacDonald, Business Owner, Pinole
Marilynne Mellander, Coordinator Save El Sobrante
